The delivery of radioactive ion beams of refractory elements using the ISOL method remains challenging, limiting access to isotopes for nuclear-structure studies. We demonstrate a method to overcome this limitation using in-trap β− decay in the ISCOOL radiofrequency quadrupole trap at CERN-ISOLDE. Radioactive parent ions are confined in helium buffer gas, where their decay products can be slowed, captured and extracted as an ion beam. Using 97,98Rb and 98Sr, we produce 97,98Sr and 98Y, monitoring their populations as a function of trapping time with the ISOLTRAP multi-reflection time-of-flight mass spectrometer. Fits to Bateman decay equations reproduce the known half-lives, validating the method and demonstrating daughter-beam efficiencies of approximately 1% relative to the initial parent intensity. We report the first delivery of a singly charged atomic 98Y beam at ISOLDE. This approach requires no modification to the existing target or ion source and opens new opportunities to study refractory isotopes that are otherwise difficult to extract.
